text:
Mattias Samuelsson is playing 23 minutes a night on a Buffalo team that has lost too often lately, and he's been one of the voices in the room about it (Heavy.com wrote up his message during the losing streak; the team's own video after the Philadelphia loss is titled "Just Too Many Turnovers"). He scored 47 seconds into that game, in the area he grew up in, and the Sabres still lost 4-3.

His season is steady more than spectacular: 3 goals and 12 points in 22 games, none on the power play, 42 blocked shots. Buffalo gets about 48% of the expected goals with him at five on five, a little worse than without him, and Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic pointed to him losing his man on a Chicago power-play goal on Nov. 12. Those are the shifts that stand out on a slumping team.

Last season was better than the reputation. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.4 wins, 20th among defensemen, most of it from even-strength offense, which is unusual for a defenseman known for hitting and blocking. Watch his five-on-five share. If it gets back to last season's level, Buffalo's defense steadies with it.
